category_title: Students with blindness and autism exhibiting executive functioning deficits and low task independence
minimal_context: The student is expected to take out their materials and begin an independent classroom assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent study. Please get your materials out and start the lesson.

STUDENT: (Sits at the desk with a very slow tempo, not reaching for any materials or initiating the task.)

TUTOR: Are you going to start working?

STUDENT: I don't know how to begin.

TUTOR: Just try to do it independently.

STUDENT: (Remains completely still, showing no inner drive to take initiative or complete the task without someone pushing the start button.)

options.A: Withhold all teacher attention from the student while they are stalling on the independent assignment.
options.B: Provide frequent opportunities to respond as a form of teacher attention during the independent assignment.
options.C: Provide detailed instructions for each specific element of the independent assignment.
options.D: Turn toward the student and issue a statement of concern, along with brief physical contact.
